Well, not really. When you convert it into a temperature increase (using the specific heat of sea water, which is about 4MJ/tonne/degree C), you end up with an increase of..... around 0.15 degrees C.

Also remember that this is all based on modelling, as they have nowhere near the amount of data required to actually measure the heat content of the ocean with any degree of accuracy. There are ~4000 Argo Buoys in the worlds' oceans. That might sound like a lot, but each one is effectively measuring an area the size of a small country (such as Portugal).

It's "irrefutable proof of global warming" that leaves no other explanation aside from the effects of human-caused heat-trapping greenhouse gas pollution, Cheng said.

Umm, no, it isn't. There are many other mechanisms that could account for an increase in the temperature of the world's oceans. Indeed, throughout the existence of the Earth, the temperature of the oceans has fluctuated quite widely without any help from humans. A couple of potential mechanisms for the increasing temperatures could be changes in cloud cover (particularly low cloud cover) and increases in volcanic activity in geologically active regions (primarily the mid ocean ridges). Changes in cloud cover are still poorly understood and are not modeled in detail within the GCM climate models since their cell size is still too large to deal with the effects of clouds. Instead, these models "parameterise" the effect of clouds, which is just a fancy way of saying they guess. Here's a brief paper out of Finland discussing a little about low clouds https://arxiv.org/pdf/1907.00165.pdf. Volcanic and other seismic activity under the Earths' oceans may impact the climate by adding heat directly to the Oceans and also by altering Ocean circulation patterns through the initiation or interruption of convective flows. There also appears to be growing evidence that sub sea volcanoes are involved in triggering El Nino events (https://www.omicsonline.org/open-access-pdfs/the-correlation-of-seismic-activity-and-recent-global-warming-2016update.pdf).
